head: Everyone said no.
Samsung bet on chips.
slides.sub: How a latecomer became the world's biggest memory maker.

image.label: A silicon wafer glowing in a clean room
image.brief: 클린룸 조명 아래 빛나는 실리콘 웨이퍼.

head: Korea was years
behind.
body: In the early 1980s, US and Japanese companies dominated memory chips. Samsung was known for TVs and appliances, and Korea had little chip expertise.

image.label: A 1980s electronics showroom full of TVs
image.brief: 1980년대 TV와 가전이 가득한 전자제품 매장. 로고 없음.

head: The Tokyo
declaration.
body: In February 1983, founder Lee Byung-chul announced in Tokyo that Samsung would make memory chips.
It was a huge, risky investment, and many inside and outside the company doubted it.

image.label: A 1983 hotel conference room in Tokyo
image.brief: 1983년 도쿄 호텔 회의실 분위기. 인물은 실루엣으로.

slides.label: Samsung's first DRAM chip, developed in 1983
body: It was years behind the leaders. But each new chip generation narrowed the gap.

image.label: A tiny early memory chip on a fingertip
image.brief: 손끝 위의 작은 초기 메모리 칩.

head: Then prices
collapsed.
body: In the mid-1980s, a glut drove memory chip prices down sharply. Samsung lost heavily on chips for several years.

image.label: A price chart falling off a cliff

head: Prices are crashing.
What now?
body: Your chip business is losing money and rivals are cutting back.

options.text: Cut losses and pull back from chips
options.feedback: It saves money now and gives up the future. Keep swiping.

options.text: Keep building plants and the next chip generation
options.feedback: This is what Samsung did. Keep swiping.
Safer, but rivals keep learning while you wait. Keep swiping.

image.label: A half-built factory at night
image.brief: 밤에 불을 켠 채 짓고 있는 반도체 공장.

head: Build in the slump,
sell in the upturn.
body: Samsung kept adding capacity while others held back. When demand recovered in the late 1980s, it had chips to sell and costs that kept falling.

image.label: New production lines lighting up
image.brief: 새 생산 라인에 하나둘 불이 켜지는 장면.

slides.label: the year Samsung says it became the world's largest DRAM maker
body: That same year it announced the first 64-megabit DRAM, according to the company. The latecomer was now leading.

image.label: A trophy-like chip on a pedestal
image.brief: 받침대 위에 놓인 칩, 정상에 오른 느낌의 조명.

head: In scale industries,
staying in wins.
body: Memory chips get cheaper to make the more you make, so the leaders keep their cost lead. Samsung accepted years of losses to climb that **learning curve** and build scale.
It traded short-term profit for a position rivals could not easily copy.

head: Leaders are often chosen
in the downturn.
body: If your industry rewards scale and experience, pulling back in a slump can cost more than the losses you avoid.
**Try it today:** what would you keep investing in even through a bad year? What could that be worth in five years?

factChecks.note: 이병철 회장의 "도쿄 선언"(1983년 2월 8일)은 삼성 공식 연혁 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1983년 2월 8일 도쿄 결정 확인(국내 보도). 공식 발표를 3월 15일로 보는 일본 자료도 있음.
64K DRAM 개발(1983년 12월)은 삼성전자 연혁 기준입니다. 개발 기간(약 6개월)은 자주 인용되지만 카드에 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1983년 12월 64K DRAM 개발 확인.
1980년대 중반 메모리 가격 폭락과 삼성 반도체 부문 누적 적자는 연구서와 보도로 확인하세요. 적자 규모는 넣지 않았습니다.

1992년 DRAM 세계 1위와 같은 해 64M DRAM 최초 개발은 삼성전자 발표 기준입니다. 시장 점유율 순위 자료(가트너·데이터퀘스트 등)로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 64M DRAM 1992년 확인. DRAM 세계 1위 연도는 1992년(회사)과 1993년(일부 자료)으로 갈려 카드에 "according to the company"를 붙임.
"생산할수록 단가가 내려간다"는 학습곡선 설명은 일반 원리이며 삼성에 대한 구체 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.
